validity.recommendation: Existence, classification, and non-duplicate status are all solidly confirmed. One open spec caveat: independently verify the 1220 mm diameter against the ORIGINAL 1997/350 km first-stage line specifically (see researcher_notes) -- the only diameter figure any independent source states outright is for the 2004+ expansion sections, not the base run.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM/gem.wiki. Uzbekistan's 1993 Cabinet of Ministers decree (lex.uz/docs/893014, decree No.389, Aug 3 1993) orders NKh 'Uzbekneftegaz' to design and build the 'magistralny gazoprovod Gazli-Nukus' (main gas pipeline Gazli-Nukus), with a first stage to Urgench commissioned in 1993. caravan.kz (2004, quoting Uzbekneftegaz's own press service) states the pipeline's first phase, 350 km long, was commissioned in 1997 and forms part of the Middle Asia-Center and Bukhara-Urals gas transport systems, then reports Uzbekneftegaz completed a second phase (66 km, 1220 mm, $50M, contractor Zeromax Group) in 2004 to raise export capacity to 7 bcm/y. studfile.net (a Russian-language academic compilation on Uzbek oil/gas projects with Russian-company participation) independently corroborates the capacity trajectory: 2004 expansion -> 7 bcm/y, then a further 2005-2006 construction phase raised capacity 'in this direction' to 12 bcm/y -- matching GEM's Capacity value exactly and via a source with no visible tie to caravan.kz. Three further, later, independent outlets (podrobno.uz and gazeta.uz, both June 2016; uzdaily.uz, English) all describe a NEW connector pipeline being built specifically to link the pre-existing, separately-named 'Gazli-Nukus' and 'Bukhara-Ural' trunk systems -- i.e. as of 2016 Gazli-Nukus was still being treated by Uzbek press as a live, distinct, operating trunk line, not a defunct or renamed one. So existence clears the bar on 4+ independent sources across 1993/2004/2016.
CLASSIFICATION: correct. Every source calls it a 'magistralny gazoprovod' (main/trunk transmission pipeline), consistent with GEM's PipelineType=transmission.
DUPLICATE: cleared. podrobno.uz/gazeta.uz/uzdaily.uz all explicitly frame Gazli-Nukus and Bukhara-Ural as TWO SEPARATE existing systems that a brand-new third pipe is built to connect -- so this is not the same physical pipe as Bukhara-Ural (P1124, excluded from this batch as Kazakhstan's row) under another name. Also distinct in corridor/endpoint from every other roster pipeline (the Gazli-Kagan family terminates short of Bukhara/Kagan; the Ahangaran-Pungan and Yangiyer-Ahangaran families are Fergana-valley lines; the Mubarek-* families are in the Kashkadarya/Bukhara corridor) -- no plausible relabel candidate.
SPEC caveat: GEM records Length=350.00 km, StartYear1=1997 -- both attested together by caravan.kz's 2004 retrospective (single source, tier medium; the 1993 decree's 'stage-1-to-Urgench-by-1993' detail is a plausible earlier construction milestone on the same corridor, not a contradiction, since Urgench sits roughly along the Gazli-Nukus route before the Karakalpakstan border). Capacity=12.00 bcm/y is corroborated to 2 decimal-matching independent sources (studfile.net explicit; caravan.kz gives the preceding 7 bcm/y step in the same buildout, corroborating the trajectory though not the final 12 figure itself) -- tier medium overall for capacity since only one source states 12 outright. Diameter=1220mm is the one figure I could NOT pin to the original 350 km stage: every independent source that gives a diameter (caravan.kz's 66 km/2004 addition; podrobno.uz/gazeta.uz/uzdaily.uz's later 74-75 km connector, which is 1020mm) is describing a LATER, DIFFERENT, shorter add-on segment, not the base 1997 line. It is plausible Soviet/Uzbek trunk-line practice re-used 1220mm for the expansion loop specifically because it matched the existing 1220mm trunk, but no source says so explicitly -- I did not find a source stating a conflicting diameter for the original run either, so this is an unconfirmed-not-contradicted caveat, not a material disagreement. Recommend checking a Uztransgaz/GIPRONIIgaz asset table if one surfaces.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched Russian-language press (2016-2026) plus Uzbek/English coverage for any decommissioning, rerouting, or abandonment of Gazli-Nukus; found none. Most recent source that names the pipeline by name and treats it as a live, in-service trunk system is the June 2016 podrobno.uz/gazeta.uz reporting on the new Gazli-Nukus<->Bukhara-Ural connector pipeline (the connector's whole rationale is boosting pressure/throughput on the Karakalpakstan/Khorezm side of the EXISTING Gazli-Nukus and Bukhara-Ural lines -- which only makes sense if both are actively carrying gas). No 2020s source names Gazli-Nukus specifically, but a 2023 gazeta.uz/spot.uz story on doubling the Gazli underground gas storage facility (3->6->10 bcm) and a reference to the 'Gazlinskoe upravlenie magistralnykh gazoprovodov' (Gazli Trunk Pipeline Administration, a Uztransgaz unit) actively working on southern-region gas-supply infrastructure both confirm the broader Gazli hub -- which Gazli-Nukus originates from -- remains a live, actively-invested national asset as of 2023, with no signal anywhere of Gazli-Nukus being idled. Given this is core domestic supply infrastructure to Karakalpakstan (Nukus is the republic's capital), not a discretionary/export project, I read the silence as ordinary (no news = no incident) rather than dormancy, and Status=operating is not stale under the annual-update rule (which targets proposed/shelved dormancy, not established operating trunk lines).

fills.researcher_notes: caravan.kz (2004) and podrobno.uz (2016) are 12 years and distinct stories apart -- one covers a capacity-expansion completion, the other a new connector construction -- both independently treat Gazli-Nukus as a live, operating trunk pipeline at their respective dates, i.e. straddling the row's StartYear1=1997 through 2016. No evidence found anywhere of interruption or decommission since.

caravan.kz 2004: 'Pervaya ochered gazoprovoda Gazli-Nukus, protyazhennostyu 350 km, byla vvedena v ekspluatatsiyu v 1997 godu' -- 'The first phase of the Gazli-Nukus pipeline, 350 km long, was commissioned in 1997.' Single independent source (tier medium); the 1993 Cabinet decree (lex.uz/docs/893014, already cited on this row for Fuel/PipelineType) is consistent context -- it orders design/construction starting 1993 with an interim milestone to Urgench that year -- but does not itself state a 1997 completion-to-Nukus date, so I did not double-count it as a second independent confirmation of the specific 1997 figure. Could not find a second source stating 1997 outright; searched Russian and English.

POLICY (source_roster.md: Wikipedia is never cited directly; studfile.net is a tertiary re-upload host, same class as the blocklisted wikidot). Downgraded from REFS_ADDED: studfile.net was the ONLY ref, so this cell is unsourced as it stands. The CLAIM is specific and likely citable elsewhere — a 2004 Gazli-Nukus section expansion raising northbound export capacity to 7 bcm/y, then 12 bcm/y after a 2005-2006 build stage. Chase it in Uzbekneftegaz/UTG annual material, Gazprom's Central Asia purchase reporting, or neftegaz.ru/interfax coverage of the 2004-2006 works. Prior note: studfile.net (Russian-language technical/academic compilation on Uzbek oil-gas projects with Russian participation): 'Rasshirenie v 2004 g. uchastka gazoprovoda Gazli-Nukus pozvolilo uvelichit eksport prirodnogo gaza v severnom napravlenii do 7 mlrd. m3, a posle vypolneniya sleduyushchego etapa stroitelstva (2005-2006 gg.) propusknaya sposobnost na etom napravlenii uvelichilas do 12 mlrd. m3 v god' -- '...capacity in this [northern] direction increased to 12 bcm/y' -- exact match to GEM's 12.00 bcm/y. caravan.kz (2004) independently corroborates the immediately preceding step of the same buildout (2004 expansion -> 7 bcm/y) but does not itself state the final 12 figure, so I am treating this as one source directly on the GEM value (tier medium) rather than double-counting caravan.kz as a second confirmation of '12' specifically.

Same caravan.kz sentence as the Start fill: first-phase/base line = 350 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown exactly. Single independent source (tier medium). Other length figures that surface in web search (43 km, 66 km, 74/75 km, 250 km, various km-post ranges) all describe DIFFERENT, later, shorter add-on/connector segments (the 2004 66 km loop; the 2016 74-75 km Gazli-Nukus<->Bukhara-Ural connector; km-post ranges for staged expansion sections) -- none of them contradicts the 350 km figure for the original 1997 base line, so this is not a spec disagreement, just a single-source result. Could not locate a second independent source stating the 350 km base figure specifically.

Could not independently confirm 1220mm for the ORIGINAL 350 km/1997 stage specifically. Every source that states a diameter ties it to a later, different, shorter segment: caravan.kz's 66 km 2004 expansion loop is 1220mm; the 2016 Gazli-Nukus<->Bukhara-Ural connector (podrobno.uz/gazeta.uz/uzdaily.uz) is a separate 74-75 km pipe at 1020mm. Neither confirms nor contradicts 1220mm for the base line. Leaving unfilled rather than citing a source that does not actually support this specific value -- see the validity spec caveat for the full reasoning.
The pipeline's own name and every source (1993 decree, caravan.kz, podrobno.uz, gazeta.uz, uzdaily.uz) confirm the Gazli gas field/hub as the origin/feed point. Two independent sources cited.

Gazli (Bukhara Region) as start and Nukus (Republic of Karakalpakstan) as end are literally the pipeline's name and confirmed by every source, including the 1993 decree naming Nukus and the Khorezm/Karakalpakstan region explicitly. Both provinces/country are correct (Gazli town is in Bukhara Region; Nukus is the capital of Karakalpakstan, an autonomous republic within Uzbekistan).

Could not find an independent source naming 'Uztransgaz' specifically as owner/operator of Gazli-Nukus. caravan.kz (2004) attributes construction financing and operation to the parent holding NKh 'Uzbekneftegaz' (Uztransgaz's predecessor for gas transport, spun off as a subsidiary later); gazligs.com confirms Uztransgaz's 'Gazliyskoe UMG' (Gazli Trunk Pipeline Administration) sits at the junction of the Bukhara-Ural, Central Asia-Center and Gazli-Chimkent trunk systems, but does not name Gazli-Nukus by name. Uztransgaz being 100% owner is plausible and consistent with it being Uzbekistan's sole national gas-transmission operator, but I would be fabricating a named-source confirmation if I cited either page for this specific cell, so leaving unresolved rather than filling.

summary: P4073 Gazli-Nukus: existence/classification/non-duplicate all independently confirmed (1993 decree + 2004 + 2016 Russian-language press); Status/Length/Capacity/StartYear/FuelSource/Location refs added (tiers high/medium); Diameter and Owner left UNRESOLVED -- no independent source ties 1220mm specifically to the original 350 km/1997 stage (only to later, different expansion segments), and no source names Uztransgaz by name for this row.
